```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
fs <- cybedtools::framework_summary
n_fw <- nrow(fs)
n_juris <- length(unique(fs$jurisdiction))
n_us <- sum(fs$jurisdiction == "US")
n_ped <- sum(fs$framework_type == "pedagogy")
ped_juris <- paste(sort(unique(fs$jurisdiction[fs$framework_type == "pedagogy"])), collapse = ", ")
```

The framework corpus splits along two axes: workforce versus
pedagogy, and jurisdiction, which now takes `r n_juris` values
(`r paste(sort(unique(fs$jurisdiction)), collapse = ", ")`). The
combinations are uneven. The US carries `r n_us` of the `r n_fw`
frameworks, and the `r n_ped` pedagogy frameworks sit in only
`r length(unique(fs$jurisdiction[fs$framework_type == "pedagogy"]))`
jurisdictions (`r ped_juris`). Together the frameworks span
the practical comparison surface for most cybersecurity workforce
and education research questions.

::: {.column-margin}
